AFWD.chosen_element: the sequential construction of the ladder product at successive rungs, together with the congruence test for a divisor equal to −1 modulo n
AFWD.justification: This forward morphism transforms the abstract existence claim into a concrete minimal witness, advancing from the first rung upward until the required divisor appears.

AREV.chosen_element: the descent from the false hypothesis that the least rung exceeds the bound, back to the known square-root growth of the ladder product
AREV.justification: The reverse morphism collapses the excessive claim under the structural constraint: the product’s size forces a divisor to appear before the given limit, thus undoing the counter-arm.

CLINK.chosen_element: the derivation of the bounding function g(n) from n — traditionally an explicit polynomial or root expression — and its attachment to the search space
CLINK.justification: Sequential chaining connects the raw integer to its bound, so that the subsequent fork can interrogate whether the least rung falls inside that bound.

ENGAGR.chosen_element: the explicit suspension of the contradiction between the just-bounded least rung and the residual possibility that a smaller bound could be falsified
ENGAGR.justification: The dialectical holding of both truth and falsity without premature resolution preserves the structural tension inherent in any minimal-witness object.

EVALF.chosen_element: the negative arm asserting that no rung up to the bound carries the required divisor, i.e., the least rung exceeds g(n)
EVALF.justification: This touches constructive falsity: the bound is alleged to be inadequate, a claim that will be overturned by the reverse morphism.

EVALT.chosen_element: the affirmative arm where the search within the bound successfully locates a rung whose ladder product contains a divisor congruent to −1 (mod n)
EVALT.justification: This touches constructive truth: the existence of a suitable rung is proven by explicit display of the divisor.

FFUSE.chosen_element: the Belnap join that merges the found minimal rung (truth) with the refutation of the unbounded claim (falsity)
FFUSE.justification: Multiplication fuses the arms into a single state where the constructive existence of the least rung and the definitive impossibility of exceeding the bound coexist — a paraconsistent B resolution.

FSPLIT.chosen_element: the bifurcation into two epistemic arms: one where a rung satisfying the divisor condition exists inside the bound, and one where the least rung lies strictly beyond the bound
FSPLIT.justification: Co-multiplication opens the problem into two possible resolutions: success within the announced limit, versus the limit being insufficient.

IFIX.chosen_element: the permanent inscription of the integer-only bound k₀ ≤ g(n) onto the object, together with the value k₀ itself
IFIX.justification: Linear fixation records the result as an irrevocable property of n; no future operation can alter or remove this bound.

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: the recognition of n as a member of the residue class 1 modulo 24, identified by the canonical representation n = 24m+1
IMSCRIB.justification: Self-reference establishes the congruence without transformation; the integer sees itself as belonging to the class that licenses the ladder algorithm.

TANCH.chosen_element: the sealed statement that the least rung k₀ satisfies k₀ ≤ g(n) and that no smaller bound can supplant this limit
TANCH.justification: This is the terminal anchor that closes the system: the result is fixed and the boundary condition n ≡ 1 (mod 24) is fully discharged.

VINIT.chosen_element: the unadorned integer n, prior to congruence verification and ladder construction
VINIT.justification: The search begins in a void where no candidate rungs or divisors have been named — the integer enters as an opaque token.

phase_2.fuse_result: a resolved state where the minimal rung k₀ is known and its bound g(n) is confirmed, while the counter-arm’s falsity is retained, yielding the Belnap value B.

The arms rejoin into a single verdict that holds both the existence of the least rung and the impossibility of exceeding the bound — B on SIXTEEN_3.

phase_3.both_description: B (11) — both held at once: the least rung exists and is bounded (truth), yet the counter-possibility of bound insufficiency is still inscribed as a surviving negation, forming a live contradiction.
phase_3.false_description: F (10) — constructively refuted: the claim that the least rung exceeds g(n) is false; the bound is sufficient.

steps.domain_action: the uninitialized integer n, congruent to 1 modulo 24, enters the system without any constructed structure.
compose n with the bounding function g(n) — for example g(n) = ⌈n^{1/2}⌉ — to delimit the search horizon.

fork on whether a rung k ≤ g(n) exists whose ladder product contains a divisor congruent to −1 modulo n; arm A will search for such a rung, arm B will entertain the possibility that no such rung exists within the bound.
arm A anchors the affirmative possibility — the existence of a suitable rung inside the bound is taken as a constructive hypothesis.
starting from rung 1, construct the ladder product, test for a divisor at −1 modulo n, and advance stepwise until the condition holds, thereby isolating the least rung k₀ ≤ g(n).
arm B anchors the negative claim — the least rung exceeds g(n), i.e., the bound is insufficient.
reverse the assumption of arm B by descending from the bound-exceedance back to the growth constraint of the ladder product, which forces the least rung to lie inside g(n).
merge the two arms: the minimal rung k₀ (truth) fuses with the impossibility of exceeding the bound (falsity) into a single paraconsistent state — B on SIXTEEN_3.
permanently record the result: the least rung k₀ and the integer-only bound k₀ ≤ g(n) are affixed as an irreversible property of n.
the system is sealed; the least rung and its bound are closed and returned as a definitive structural object.

phase_5.ipc_mechanism: The current rung index and the accumulated product are passed between construction steps through a single mutable register updated at each iteration.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: A local store holds the ladder product at the current rung and the tested divisor candidates, discarding earlier rungs once a success is found.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: A strictly monotonic itinerary governs the order: rung 1, then 2, then 3, … up to g(n), with an immediate halt when the divisor appears — no reordering or concurrency.

phase_6.cycle_cost: One modular multiplication and one greatest-common-divisor test per rung, scaling with the bound g(n).
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the information gained (one minimal index and a bound) exactly mirrors the latency of the search, because the bound function encodes the structural complexity of the congruence class, leaving no unaccounted entropy.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: The least rung k₀ is identified and the bound k₀ ≤ g(n) is permanently inscribed; the search space is collapsed to this witness.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: The integer n is given, but no rungs have been evaluated; the ladder product is empty and the bound is unattached.
